vars.name: ENV

vars.name: SECRET_KEY
vars.description: JWT signing + key encryption

vars.name: DOMAIN
vars.description: dashboard hostname (Caddy auto-TLS)

vars.name: API_DOMAIN
vars.description: API hostname (Caddy auto-TLS)

vars.name: ACME_EMAIL
vars.description: Let's Encrypt contact email

vars.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
vars.description: prod: https://$API_DOMAIN (baked into the web build)

vars.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_N8N_URL
vars.description: prod: https://n8n.<your-domain> (baked into the web build; the "Open n8n" link)

vars.name: BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS
vars.description: nightly pg_dump retention (prod backup service)

sections.name: Datastores (compose sets these to in-network hosts automatically)

vars.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
vars.description: Choose a strong password — "vicero" is the first thing anyone tries. Generate one with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(30))" and use the SAME value in DATABASE_URL below. Compose refuses to start without it.

vars.name: REDIS_PASSWORD
vars.description: 127.0.0.1, not localhost: the dev containers publish on IPv4 loopback only, and localhost tries IPv6 first. Password for the dev Redis (compose refuses to start without it). Generate one the same way as POSTGRES_PASSWORD above and use the SAME value inside REDIS_URL.

sections.name: LLM providers (free-first). Unset → provider stubbed + warned.

vars.name: GROQ_API_KEY
vars.description: default provider (free signup)

vars.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
vars.description: Google Gemini free tier

vars.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
vars.description: free models via OpenRouter

vars.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
vars.description: paid

vars.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
vars.description: paid

vars.name: OLLAMA_BASE_URL
vars.description: local models + embeddings (bundled)

vars.name: PROVIDER_PRIVATE_HOSTS
vars.description: Private/LAN hosts a *tenant-set* provider endpoint (Settings -> Provider keys -> Custom endpoint, or an Ollama/Mistral/... URL override) may point at. Empty = tenants can only reach public endpoints. Comma-separated exact hostnames or IPs, e.g. host.docker.internal,10.0.0.5. Operator-only: never expose this to tenants. Does not affect OLLAMA_BASE_URL above.

vars.name: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER
vars.description: `openai` and `gemini` are accepted here and then routed to Ollama anyway - no adapter for either was ever written. Startup warns if you set one, because there is otherwise no symptom.

vars.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
vars.description: 768 dimensions, which is what the `chunks.embedding` column is. A model with a different dimension needs a migration, not just this line.

vars.name: EMBEDDING_PROBE_ENABLED
vars.description: One HTTP GET at startup: does the embedding endpoint answer, and does it have the model pulled? It exists because prod pointed at an `ollama` service that was never declared, so every ingest failed with nothing looking wrong (docs/15 PROD-2). Never fails startup; ~2s worst case.

vars.name: FACEBOOK_CLIENT_ID
vars.description: Facebook Login (Meta for Developers app). Redirect URI: {OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE}/v1/auth/oauth/facebook/callback — see docs/ENV.md.

vars.name: SELF_SERVE_ENABLED
vars.description: Master switch. true: signing up creates one 10-day trial workspace (500 messages, one agent, no workflows / n8n / tool calling). false: workspaces are created by staff only, as before — also the kill switch if signups are being abused. The plan limits themselves live in apps/api/app/core/plans.py, not here.

vars.name: SIGNUPS_PER_IP_PER_DAY
vars.description: New self-serve accounts allowed per client IP per 24h. 0 disables the cap.

vars.name: BLOCK_DISPOSABLE_EMAILS
vars.description: Refuse throwaway-mailbox domains (mailinator, yopmail, …) at signup. Turn off for internal use.

vars.name: DISPOSABLE_MX_CHECK_ENABLED
vars.description: Where the maintained throwaway-domain list comes from (refreshed weekly by Celery beat — run beat). DISPOSABLE_LIST_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/disposable-email-domains/disposable-email-domains/main/disposable_email_blocklist.conf Record (never block on) addresses whose mail servers don't exist or belong to a throwaway service.

vars.name: TRUSTED_PROXIES
vars.description: Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For the API trusts to say who the visitor is (IPs / CIDRs). Without this every visitor behind the web app is one address and every per-IP limit is one shared bucket. The compose files set the Docker range for you. NEVER put a public range here.

vars.name: LOGIN_LOCKOUT_FAILURES
vars.description: Failed password logins per email before that address is locked out, and for how long (seconds).

vars.name: ORG_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT
vars.description: Public chat messages per minute per organization on a metered plan, so one bot cannot burn a whole trial in seconds. Messages past it get no reply (silently) and are not counted.

vars.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_UPGRADE_EMAIL
vars.description: Where the Upgrade page sends people until paid plans exist (web app; both optional). Baked in at build time. WhatsApp is digits only, with country code.

sections.name: Channels (unset → channel disabled with a clear message)

vars.name: META_APP_SECRET
vars.description: shared by WhatsApp + Messenger + Instagram; also verifies the Data Deletion Request Callback (empty = 503)

vars.name: META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN
vars.description: Facebook Messenger page token

vars.name: META_PAGE_ID
vars.description: the Page that receives Messenger DMs

vars.name: INSTAGRAM_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN
vars.description: Instagram-scoped page token (instagram_manage_messages)

vars.name: INSTAGRAM_USER_ID
vars.description: the Instagram professional account id

vars.name: META_VERIFY_TOKEN
vars.description: you choose; echoed back during Meta's webhook handshake. Also the single verify token of the shared webhook (/api/meta/webhook) used by one-click connect

vars.name: META_APP_ID
vars.description: One-click connect for WhatsApp / Messenger / Instagram (docs/26). It is enabled only when META_APP_ID, META_APP_SECRET and META_VERIFY_TOKEN are all set; WhatsApp also needs the Embedded Signup configuration id. App ID of the Meta app (developers.facebook.com -> App settings -> Basic). Public value.

vars.name: META_EMBEDDED_SIGNUP_CONFIG_ID
vars.description: Facebook Login for Business -> Configurations -> the WhatsApp Embedded Signup configuration id

vars.name: META_GRAPH_VERSION
vars.description: Graph API version used by every Meta call (adapters + connect flow)

vars.name: META_APP_LIVE
vars.description: Set true once Meta has approved the app; until then the UI tells customers only testers can connect

vars.name: N8N_BASE_URL
vars.description: must match the bundled n8n's host port

vars.name: N8N_API_KEY
vars.description: The bundled n8n's host port is `N8N_HOST_PORT` (default 5678) — but note that Compose reads *interpolation* variables from the shell or from `infra/.env`, NOT from this file (this file is passed to containers via `env_file`). So to move it: cd infra && N8N_HOST_PORT=5679 docker compose up -d n8n # or put it in infra/.env then set N8N_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5679 here. n8n → Settings → API; needs the workflow read/list/create/update/activate scopes

vars.name: N8N_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
vars.description: generate a random string. n8n workflows VERIFY this (docs/07). THIS FILE IS ITS ONE HOME: the api, worker and the n8n container all read it from here — do NOT copy it into infra/.env. Start n8n with `make up` (or `docker compose --env-file .env --env-file ../.env ...` from infra/) so Compose can interpolate it into the n8n container; started without that, n8n gets an empty secret and rejects every call (fail closed) — see infra/n8n/README.md "Why one file".

vars.name: N8N_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE_CHECK
vars.description: Refuse to bind an n8n tool whose workflow would accept an UNSIGNED call (no verify chain — R15). On by default; the pasted-URL path is resolved through the n8n API, so it also needs N8N_API_KEY. Turn off only for a deliberately unsigned dev n8n.

vars.name: AUTOMATION_REPORT_SECRET
vars.description: HMAC secret n8n uses to sign run reports to POST /internal/automations/runs. Unset = that endpoint answers 503 and nothing is recorded. In production `ops/n8n-setup.sh` generates it; here, generate a random string.

vars.name: N8N_REQUIRE_REGISTERED_AUTOMATION
vars.description: An n8n tool may be bound to / run a webhook only if it belongs to a registered, Active automation of the same org and agent. Leave true; false is for a keyless dev n8n with no registry.

vars.name: AUTOMATION_PULL_ENABLED
vars.description: Celery beat job (every 5 min) that fills gaps in the run log from the n8n API. Needs N8N_API_KEY.

vars.name: VICERO_API_BASE_URL
vars.description: One command stands a client up: org + published agent + n8n automation + invite. Identical on a laptop and on a VPS — only these URLs differ.

vars.name: PROVISION_STAFF_EMAIL
vars.description: a staff login (is_staff=true). Creating an org is gated on that flag server-side, so an API key cannot provision — there is no such scope.

vars.name: PROVISION_STAFF_PASSWORD
vars.description: that account's password

sections.name: Email (console backend needs no setup in dev)

vars.name: EMAIL_BACKEND
vars.description: console = logged to an in-memory outbox, nothing leaves the machine. smtp = real delivery. Any SMTP relay works — Resend and Postmark both have a free tier that suits a first handful of clients. You must also verify your sending domain (SPF/DKIM records) in the provider's dashboard, or Gmail will spam-bin it. — console | smtp — set smtp once SMTP_* below are filled in

vars.name: SMTP_HOST
vars.description: e.g. smtp.resend.com — any SMTP relay works

vars.name: SMTP_USER
vars.description: from your email provider

vars.name: SMTP_PASS
vars.description: from your email provider

vars.name: SMTP_FROM
vars.description: e.g. "Vicero <noreply@yourdomain.com>"

vars.name: SENTRY_DSN
vars.description: optional

vars.name: STORAGE_BACKEND
vars.description: local | s3

vars.name: UPLOAD_DIR
vars.description: where ingested document files are stored (local backend)

vars.name: RAG_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET
vars.description: max chars of retrieved context injected into a prompt

vars.name: RAG_RRF_FTS_WEIGHT
vars.description: Weight of the keyword (FTS) list in the hybrid RRF fusion; dense is fixed at 1.0. Conservative on purpose - see ADR-058. Re-fit with `make eval-retrieval-full` on a real KB.

vars.name: CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER
vars.description: true = run ingestion inline (no worker); dev/testing only

vars.name: DOCLING_ENABLED
vars.description: Replaces the flat pypdf text stream with real headings, reading order, table structure and OCR. Runs in the Celery worker, so it cannot affect chat latency. OFF by default; roll out per docs/14 §12. Any failure falls back to the legacy extractor, so a Docling outage never marks a client's upload as broken.

vars.name: DOCLING_ENDPOINT
vars.description: INTERNAL address only. NEVER publish this service's port (docs/14 §9) - it accepts arbitrary documents and URLs, so a public port is SSRF plus resource exhaustion. Compose sets this on the worker automatically; set it here only when pointing at an external instance.

vars.name: DOCLING_DO_OCR
vars.description: scanned PDFs stop being "no extractable text"

vars.name: DOCLING_DO_TABLE_STRUCTURE
vars.description: a pricing table stops becoming word soup

vars.name: DOCLING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
vars.description: Docling's own guidance is 90-120s

vars.name: DOCLING_CHUNK_MAX_TOKENS
vars.description: tokens per chunk, not characters. Sweepable (docs/14 K2-5)

vars.name: DOCLING_CHUNK_HEADING_MODE
vars.description: Where the heading path goes: `embed` (embedding input only) or `inline` (also into the stored chunk a visitor sees quoted). Leave it on `embed`: since migration 0021 the FTS index covers heading + content, so both modes score the same and `inline` only costs citation cleanliness. See ADR-065 for the measurement that forced the option and ADR-067 for the one that settled it.

vars.name: MAX_PDF_PAGES
vars.description: Page cap for PDF ingest (docs/14 K5-2). 0 disables. A backstop against the pathological case, not a product limit - a real client manual runs to a few hundred pages and must still ingest.

sections.name: Reranking: stage 4 of retrieval (docs/13 R1, ADR-063)

vars.name: RERANK_ENABLED
vars.description: A cross-encoder reorders the fused candidates. OFF platform-wide AND per agent; both must be on. It costs a round trip BEFORE the first token, so enabling it is a latency decision. Any failure degrades to RRF ordering - never an error, never an empty result.

vars.name: RERANK_ENDPOINT
vars.description: A /rerank endpoint. Self-hosted text-embeddings-inference is recommended: client KB text never leaves the deployment, and bge-reranker-v2-m3 is trained multilingual. Enabled with this empty warns at startup and silently falls back to RRF order.

vars.name: RERANK_CANDIDATE_K
vars.description: fused candidates handed to the cross-encoder

vars.name: RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS
vars.description: on timeout the turn proceeds on RRF ordering

vars.name: RERANK_API_KEY
vars.description: PLATFORM credential, never a client's (ADR-063). A self-hosted TEI container needs none. optional - only for a hosted rerank API

vars.name: LLM_FORCE_FAKE
vars.description: true = force every chat/embedding onto the Fake provider (E2E/CI only; NEVER prod)

vars.name: WEBHOOK_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS
vars.description: how often Celery beat re-enqueues due pending webhook deliveries

vars.name: MEMORY_WINDOW_MESSAGES
vars.description: recent turns kept verbatim in the prompt

vars.name: MEMORY_SUMMARY_THRESHOLD
vars.description: summarize older turns once a convo exceeds this many msgs

vars.name: SUMMARY_PROVIDER
vars.description: provider for background summaries (small/fast, NOT the agent's)

vars.name: SUMMARY_MODEL
vars.description: summary model; falls back to the fake provider if unkeyed

vars.name: TOOL_MAX_ITERATIONS
vars.description: Opt-in: makes tests/test_default_model.py ask Groq itself whether the platform default models still exist (needs a real GROQ_API_KEY; a few tokens). Off by default so CI never depends on a vendor. RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1 — max tool-call iterations per turn (Phase 9)

vars.name: TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
vars.description: per-tool execution timeout (Phase 9)

vars.name: AGENTIC_LOOP_ENABLED
vars.description: Platform-wide gate for the chat agentic loop / MCP tools. Off here AND per-org (Organization.agentic_loop_enabled) by default - both must be explicitly on.

vars.name: AGENTIC_MAX_STEPS
vars.description: AgentBudget ceiling shared by the chat agentic loop AND every workflow run (a nested call decrements the SAME budget, never a fresh one - docs/17 §2 rule 3).

vars.name: MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
vars.description: Wider than TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: an MCP call is a subprocess spawn or a 3rd-party round trip.

vars.name: WORKFLOW_MAX_CALL_DEPTH
vars.description: How deep a chain of workflow sub_agent nodes may nest before AgentBudget.call_depth trips it.

vars.name: WORKFLOW_MAX_DELAY_SECONDS
vars.description: Longest a workflow delay node may schedule a real wait for (seconds, default 24h). Rejected loudly above this, never silently clamped.

vars.name: MAX_USER_MESSAGE_CHARS
vars.description: Hard ceiling on one visitor message; also the LLM10 unbounded-consumption control.

vars.name: GUARD_INPUT_ENABLED
vars.description: L1 static pre-filter on the visitor's own message (direct prompt injection, OWASP LLM01). Off means retrieved content is defended but the person typing is not.

vars.name: GUARD_OUTPUT_ENABLED
vars.description: L5 output guardrail: system-prompt leakage and persona breaks.

vars.name: GUARD_OUTPUT_LEAK_THRESHOLD
vars.description: Fraction of a reply's 8-grams that may also appear in the system prompt before it is treated as leakage and replaced.

vars.name: GUARD_PII_EGRESS_ENABLED
vars.description: L5 PII egress: redact emails/phones from a reply unless the org has allowlisted them in Organization.public_contacts. Secret redaction runs regardless of this flag.

vars.name: GUARD_PII_PHONE_REGIONS
vars.description: Regions used to read phone numbers written WITHOUT a country code, most likely first. Numbers written with an explicit +CC are found regardless of this list.

vars.name: GUARD_PII_REDACT_ADDRESSES
vars.description: Street-address detection is much less precise than email/phone ("12 Month Plan" reads as a house number), so it is counted in a document's pii_flags but not redacted from replies.

vars.name: GUARD_INJECTION_ENABLED
vars.description: Catches what the L1 regexes structurally cannot: paraphrase, and every language other than English. Runs on the PLATFORM GROQ_API_KEY, never a client's key (ADR-055) - so it keeps working for an org running its agent on Mistral/DeepSeek/xAI/etc.

vars.name: GUARD_INJECTION_MODEL
vars.description: Model id, never inline: Groq deprecated llama-guard-4-12b in Feb 2026. Check https://console.groq.com/docs/deprecations before changing this.

vars.name: GUARD_INJECTION_THRESHOLD
vars.description: Measured separation is huge (benign < 0.005, attacks > 0.998), so 0.5 sits in empty space.

vars.name: GUARD_INJECTION_TIMEOUT_MS
vars.description: On timeout the turn proceeds UNGUARDED (fail open) with a loud log and a metric.

sections.name: L3 policy & distress classifier (docs/11 §4-L3, Phase E)

vars.name: GUARD_POLICY_ENABLED
vars.description: Grades each customer message against the markdown in apps/api/app/chat/policies/ (editable, hot-reloadable). Drives the inbox "Needs attention" queue. Runs on the PLATFORM key. NOTE: on `elevated` the bot KEEPS ANSWERING while a human is alerted. Only `crisis` suppresses the reply, and it emits a fixed written holding message - never silence.

vars.name: GUARD_DISTRESS_ENABLED
vars.description: Turn distress grading off entirely for a client who has not agreed to watch the queue.

vars.name: WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED
vars.description: OFF by default and off per-agent too. Enabling it lets an agent reach the open internet on a customer's behalf, which is a per-client decision, not a platform default. The per-agent domain allowlist (features.web_search_allowed_domains) ships EMPTY, and empty means NOTHING is searchable - not "search anything". A support agent that can search the whole web will confidently quote a competitor's pricing.

vars.name: WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY
vars.description: Tavily (or any endpoint returning {results:[{url,title,content}]})

vars.name: VAULT_ADMIN_EMAILS
vars.description: A separate sign-in, entirely independent of Vicero accounts, that shows the internal architecture and the real values of every setting in this file (masked until revealed). It stays OFF until all three are set. Run `make vault-password` to generate the hash and the session secret — it never prints or stores the password itself. Comma-separated allow-list. Only these addresses may sign in.

vars.name: VAULT_PASSWORD_HASH
vars.description: Output of `make vault-password`. A hash, never the password.

vars.name: VAULT_SESSION_SECRET
vars.description: Random, 32+ characters. Signs the session cookie. Changing it signs the admin out.

vars.name: VAULT_ENV_FILE
vars.description: Optional path to a KEY=value file (e.g. a read-only mount of the root .env) to read values from when they are not in the web process's own environment. The dev compose already gives the web container the whole root .env; the production one gives it two variables only.

sections.name: Test-only switches (NEVER set these in production)

vars.name: ALLOW_SELF_SERVE_ORGS
vars.description: Lets a non-staff user create an organization. Production is staff-only: Vicero is provisioned per client, and with this on anyone who can reach /signup can hand themselves a workspace. The test suites need it because they bootstrap a tenant per test via the API.

vars.name: TRUST_GEO_HEADERS
vars.description: Country header -> display currency on GET /v1/billing/plans. DISPLAY ONLY: never decides what is charged or what plan an org gets. Leave false in dev. Set true in prod ONLY when the API is reachable solely through a proxy that sets one of the headers below (otherwise it is spoofable).

vars.name: GEO_COUNTRY_HEADERS
vars.description: Comma-separated, checked in order; first non-empty known country wins.

vars.name: GEOIP_DB_PATH
vars.description: Offline IP->country database (no key needed): `python scripts/fetch_geoip_db.py` from apps/api, then set this to the file it wrote. Used only when no trusted header gave a country - works with plain Caddy. Display only. Empty = off. Needs TRUSTED_PROXIES set so the visitor's X-Forwarded-For is believed.
